tests/flow/launcher.ts uses the child process 'exit' event (not 'close') to resolve the exit promise that startFlowApp's stop()/restartWeb() await, while webDiagnosticForwarder relies on a separate 'data'/'end' listener on the same stderr stream. Node's own documentation notes 'exit' can fire before stdio streams finish delivering buffered data, which is a theoretical (unconfirmed by execution) ordering hazard for end-of-stream diagnostic flushing in general, though in the specific tests/readiness/staff-diagnostic.ts regression the diagnostic write and app.stop() call are separated by multiple awaited DB round-trips, making the race window negligible in that concrete test as evidenced by consistent PASS/exit0 in both local Mac and CI Linux logs.

webDiagnosticForwarder decodes each stderr chunk independently via Buffer.from(chunk).toString('utf8') before iterating characters; a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence split exactly across two chunk boundaries would be decoded as replacement characters in each fragment rather than reconstructed. This cannot corrupt the intended pure-ASCII AUTH_PIPELINE_CODE / STAFF_OPERATION_DIAGNOSTIC schema (such corruption would just fail the strict schema match and be safely dropped, which is the designed fail-closed behavior), so it is noted only as a robustness observation, not a demonstrated defect, and not independently verified by execution.
